tests.description: write into a dir that does not exist, with a filename two folders deep, creates every folder and the file reads back.
writeBinary creates missing folders the same way.
The std::write payload names the folder that would be created, and rejecting the write leaves it uncreated.
A write whose path runs through an existing file is refused with a message that says so, and no std::write is raised.
A redirected echo through safeBash into a folder that does not exist still fails, as in bash, and creates no folder.
edit, which shares write's path preparation, still refuses a dir that does not exist before raising its interrupt.
